title: Audit timeline and change-blame contract for RBAC v2 & SSO admin operations
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Define a durable, queryable audit event contract that supports a timeline view and robust change-blame for RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML admin operations. This ticket captures the proposed event fields, taxonomy for what to log (actor, target, intent, outcome), the recommended compact diff encoding for permission/model changes, sampling/retention guidance, and a migration approach for existing audit consumers (console, billing, compliance exports).
background: RBAC v2 introduces fine-grained policy objects and multi-step admin flows (role composition, dynamic grants, delegated admin). Current audit shape is inconsistent across services and lacks a deterministic way to attribute a state change to a single initiating actor when system automation or multi-step UIs participate. We need an audit timeline model that preserves both the authoritative change frame (before/after) and the operational lineage (who or what ultimately caused the change).
goals: Provide a single event contract usable by Console, Private control plane, and Dedicated admin APIs
Encode a compact, diff-first change payload for permission/resource updates to minimize storage while preserving reconstructability
Expose blame and lineage fields to resolve attribution for automated rollouts, orchestration, and delegated admin actions
Ensure SSO/SAML-linked events surface identity provider metadata for compliance and incident investigations
Define migration compatibility for existing audit consumers and retention tiers
non_goals: Full-text logging of entire resource objects for every event (we prefer compact diffs + optional snapshots)
Replacing external SIEM normalization rules (we provide a stable contract to integrate with SIEMs)
Changing existing RBAC semantics: this is an observability contract, not an access model redesign
event_taxonomy_summary: Three axis taxonomy: (1) Intent (admin.change, admin.create, admin.delete, auth.assertion, config.change), (2) Actor identity metadata (type, id, idp, auth_method), (3) Target & change payload (resource type, compact diff, optional full snapshot). Additional orthogonal labels: outcome, sensitivity (PII/secret footprint), and compliance tags (gdpr/sox).
diff_encoding_proposal: Use a compact-diff-v1 canonical format: canonicalize JSON by stable key ordering -> compute field-level ops (add/modify/remove) with path-addressing (dot/bracket) -> store op list as a compressed newline-delimited text blob. Include before_digest and after_digest (sha256 over canonicalized object) for quick integrity checks. For large structural changes, include optional snapshot references (immutable storage) instead of embedding full states.
actor_target_model: Actors must carry both asserted identity and provenance: asserted_id (e.g., user@example.com), id_type (user|service), idp metadata (idp_id, assertion_id), and session context (session_id, trace_id). Targets should have resource_type, canonical_id, and stable version or digest. This allows joins across events to reconstruct timelines and to attribute changes when intermediaries (automation) perform the actual write.
retention_and_sampling_policy: Default retention: 90 days for 'audit' tier, 7 days for 'shortterm' operational tier, and 7 years for 'compliance' tier where required. Sampling allowed for high-volume low-sensitivity events (e.g., auth.success) with deterministic sampling keys (actor_id + day) and clear sampling_reason stored in the event. Critical admin.change and SSO assertion failures must never be sampled.
acceptance_criteria: Core event contract document merged in RFC and surfaced to Console and Private control plane teams
Examples and 3 sample events (role create, permission delta, sso-failed-login) added to the spec
Console timeline UI team confirms fields required for change-blame story are emitted by backend mocks
Migration plan with consumer compatibility steps and a small shim library for encoding/decoding provided
Security review completed and compliance retention tiers mapped to legal requirements
updates: 2025-02-10: Draft created and cross-team RFC posted to #sec-architecture.
2025-02-12: Embedded proposed compact-diff encoding after sync with runtime team; added before/after digest fields.
2025-02-14: QA and Console owners requested explicit 'lineage.steps' field to link UI actions across background jobs — added to schema.
2025-02-16: Compliance asked for retention_class and storage_ref fields; included and noted legal mapping task.
2025-02-18: Assigned to Maya for engineering implementation plan and sample shims; set target due_date 2025-02-28.
decisions: Adopt compact-diff-v1 as primary change encoding; optional full snapshots stored by reference.
Make SSO identity_provider metadata required for idp-authenticated events.
Never sample admin.change events; allow deterministic sampling only on high-volume non-admin auth events.
migration_steps: 1) Add new event emission path alongside existing audit events (dual-write) for 6 weeks.
2) Provide shim library (python/node) to transform old events to new contract for consumers that cannot dual-read yet.
3) Run consumer compatibility tests and deprecate old fields after 6 weeks of no-blocker findings.
4) Enable retention tiering and export scripts for Compliance team to pull long-term archives.
